title: And Ben Platt, who played Last, he gave everything #TheLastFiveYears ...
transcript: Okay, let's talk about Rachel Zegler and Ben Platt in the last five years at Radio City Music Hall, because sorry to the haters, but I loved it. I loved it. Do I think that this is the optimal way to see the last five years? No. This show is always going to work better in smaller, intimate theatres. But as far as a concert presentation of this material goes, I think this is about as good as it gets. Especially when you have the likes of Rachel Zegler proving once again that she is a freaking mega star. Despite the fact that this is a concert production, she is giving a full Tony Award worthy performance, and vocally, it may be the best the role has ever been sung. I also really liked having a noticeably younger Jamie and Cathy, because both of these characters are deeply immature and so much of their actions in the show do make sense once you consider, oh, yeah, they're young. And this is compounded with the fact that Ben Platt plays a very sympathetic Jamie. So I think you're really able to see the fault on both sides. I know a lot of people have not been as high on Ben Platt's performance, and I do think in general, he seems to be prioritising his vocal performance over his acting performance. Especially in the latter half when he's doing his more serious songs. He is riffing up a storm and it sounds great. But it definitely does come at the expense of the emotional authenticity of the moment. But also, I feel like that is what a concert production is supposed to be. It is supposed to be vocals first. And so I don't really mind this approach. I think it only feels a little bit jarring because he is up against Rachel Zegler, who is giving this fully realised performance. But no doubt this is going to become my go to cast album for this score. There are also some lyric changes in this production, most of which were carryovers from the recent Broadway revival. So in summer in Ohio, they've removed the derogatory term for a little person and it's now a gay dentist named Carl playing Tevya and porgy. There are also some new lyrics in Shiksa Goddess, which I think work fine. And there are also some new lyrics in A Miracle Would Happen, which I decidedly don't like. Bring back the old lyrics, Jason, please. But besides that, I do like all of the lyrical updates and the score does sound gorgeous. With this expanded band, this score has really never sounded better.
